answer: Remote attestation from a TEE proves which code ran, and each submission carries a fresh nonce so a captured quote cannot be replayed by a second account. Because disagreement between peer reviewers dilutes the weight of the attestation, a farm running identical enclosures on one ledge casts correlated votes that cancel each other. Fifty cloned machines earn less than one. A new quill does not make a copied quote useful when the nonce changes, and the karst of cheap hardware stops being a shortcut.
